findings.reason: the plan should extend review_path/plan_review_path to accept the committed state root rather than mint a parallel resolver in ledger.py.
findings.text: §3 places review-path composition in reckon/ledger.py, but reckon/crew/review.py:1242 review_path and reckon/crew/plan_review.py:330 plan_review_path already own how a review path is composed (keyed by reviewed run id with an .at-<sha> sibling, and by plan slug/version with an .at-<blob8> sibling), and reckon/_store.py:215 state_path owns the docs/state/<project>/ rule that ledger_path (reckon/ledger.py:618) already delegates to; a review-path rule added to ledger.py is a third path rule beside the two that exist, exactly the fork the section's own text disowns ("not by a second path rule")

findings.reason: the plan should cite the existing importer and reuse or extend its pattern rather than propose a parallel one without saying what it searched.
findings.text: §5 adds scripts/import_review_store.py to parse a host store, deduplicate by identity and re-run idempotently, but the repository already carries scripts/import_runs_into_store.py doing the same host-store-to-store import over the crew ledger, and a reusable importer returning per-project counts already exists there as the shape this plan reinvents

findings.reason: the section must account for the refusal surface it adds, as the rubric holds every section that adds to a tracked family to do.
findings.text: §7 makes crew review-plan refuse on a hold, the sweep skip a held plan and the gate refuse a build of it, and adds a plan-review-hold scalar merged into PLAN_METADATA_SCALARS, adding to the refusal surface (refusal_families 23) without naming any refusal it retires or merges, or stating why none can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3 hides the record shape, the committed store and the committed-first join behind one store function (store_delivered_reviews) and one reader extending reckon/crew/review.py, and §4 derives the lifecycle in Python rather than storing it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 resolves the committed review path through reckon/ledger.py and calls it "the owner of the committed state tree", but review-path composition is already owned by review.review_path/review_store_root and plan_review.plan_review_path, and the docs/state/<project> rule is owned by _store.state_path, which ledger_path already delegates to.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §7 adds refusal conditions (the sweep skips a held plan, crew review-plan refuses, the gate refuses a build) and a new plan-metadata scalar without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites ledger.py, review.py, plan_review.py, promotion.py and recovery.py for the code it extends, but §5 adds a one-shot host-store import script without citing the existing scripts/import_runs_into_store.py, which is the same host-store-to-store import shape.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 changes where the existing store function writes, §4 folds a summary into the existing crew(view="plan-review") rather than adding a view, and §7 reuses the existing set op and PLAN_METADATA_SCALARS exclusion set; each is an extension, and each says so.
